newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA RECOVER TO BEAT AIK STOCKHOLM 3-1.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA RECOVER TO BEAT AIK STOCKHOLM 3-1.

text.p: Gheorghe Popescu, Ronaldo and Juan Pizzi saved the blushes of Barcelona team mate Carlos Busquets on Thursday by bringing their team back from a first-minute deficit to beat AIK Stockholm 3-1 in their Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final first leg.
A huge gaffe from reserve keeper Busquets allowed Pascal Simpson to score in the first minute but the home side struck straight back and could easily have put six past the Swedes.
Fans had hardly taken their seats at the Camp Nou when the ball was passed back to Busquets, who last season was heavily criticised for using his feet too much while still a first choice.
This time his control let him down, and Simpson thundered in to give his side an unexpected lead.
But directly from the re-start Barcelona won a free-kick on the left. Josep Guardiola took it and captain Popescu emerged at the far post to head home the equaliser.

Barcelona quickly took control of the game, but missed a series of chances and ran out of steam before half-time. Busquets was booed from the start, and the crowd also became impatient with other players, among them star striker Ronaldo.

After twice being denied by Magnesia Headman in the first half, Ronaldo silenced his critics by leaving the Swedish keeper stranded with a superb header from a Hristo Stoichkov cross shortly after the break.
Stoichkov was substituted midway through the second half and reacted angrily, hurling abuse towards the Barcelona bench.
Ronaldo continued to supply the fireworks on the field, and unselfishly set up the third for strike partner Juan Pizzi 15 minutes from time.

Both sides were reduced to ten men at the end of a generally good-tempered game when Barca's French international Laurent Blanc was given a red card for preventing a run on goal, while the visitorseived his second booking for a tackle from behind.
Barcelona's Luis Enrique Martinez picked up his second yellow card of the competition and will miss the return game in two weeks.
Barcelona fans will hope that regular keeper Vitor Baia is fully fit by then although Busquets did something to redeem himself by fending off a rare Swedish attack in the dying minutes.

Manager Bobby Robson will hope progress in this competition lift pressure on him that has been growing in recent months. Earlier on Thursday Real Betis beat Sporting Gijon 4-2 to draw level on points with his team as the race for a second Champions' League place hots up.
